en.title: Lexicographically Smallest Message After Right-Rotating One Substring
en.description:
Choose exactly one non-empty substring and rotate it right by 1, i.e. move its last character to the front and shift the other characters right. Find the lexicographically smallest resulting string. Choosing a single character, which leaves the string unchanged, is allowed.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: One line containing a lowercase string of length 1..100000.
en.explanation: The answers are aaahhb, abc and acbab.
hints: Scanning from the right, maintain the minimum character of each suffix and its rightmost position. Find the earliest position that can be improved by a smaller character further right, and move the rightmost occurrence of that suffix minimum to this position.
